content.title: About
content.content: Salisbury steak is a seasoned ground beef patty shaped like a steak and served with a rich brown gravy made from beef broth, onions, carrots, and tomato paste. The dish originated in the United States in the early 20th century and became popular for its hearty flavor and ease of preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “Salisbury steak” comes from Dr. James H. Salisbury, a 19th‑century physician who promoted minced beef as a health food.
Traditional gravy is thickened with a roux of butter and flour, giving it a smooth, velvety texture.
In the U.S. it is commonly served with mashed potatoes or egg noodles, while in the UK it is sometimes called a “ground beef steak”.
There are many sauce variations, from classic brown gravy to tomato‑wine mushroom sauces.
Salisbury steak is a staple in school cafeterias and military mess halls because it is nutritious and inexpensive.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Ground beef provides a complete source of high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Salisbury steak supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Calcium from gravy
items.content: When dairy or fortified broth is used in the gravy, the dish adds extra calcium.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: The meal is suitable for low‑carbohydrate diets when served without starchy sides.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Ground beef can be high in saturated fats, which should be limited in heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Sodium in gravy
items.content: Gravy often contains added salt or soy sauce, increasing overall sodium intake.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper cooking of ground beef can lead to salmonella or E. coli contamination.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergy or intolerance to beef.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Shape the seasoned ground beef into 2‑3 cm thick patties, sear them on high heat until browned, then simmer in the gravy for 15–20 minutes until cooked through. For the gravy, sauté onions and carrots, stir in flour, then add beef broth, tomato paste, and seasonings. Serve with mashed potatoes, rice, or a vegetable side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked Salisbury steak in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C to ensure safety.
